summary: Describes the Hostnames Server, a service that delivers machine-readable name and address information about networks, gateways and hosts. Replaced by RFC 953.

plainLanguage.summary: The Hostnames Server answers text queries for records about networks, gateways and hosts. The RFC calls the central database an interim solution on the way to a distributed service, and RFC 953 later replaced this specification.

questions: how to get host name table from server
subtitle: A text query service for looking up internet host names and addresses

tldr.problem: Programs needed machine-readable name and address information for internet networks, gateways and hosts.
tldr.mechanism: A client connects to SRI-NIC, sends HNAME, HADDR or ALL, and reads a response containing host-table records.
tldr.outcome: The RFC describes the centrally managed table as an interim step toward a distributed name and address service; RFC 953 later replaced it.

sections.title: The Hostnames Server
sections.content:
The NIC Internet Hostnames Server runs on SRI-NIC and provides machine-readable name and address information about networks, gateways and hosts. The document says it may eventually include domains. Its entries follow the DoD Internet Host Table Specification in RFC 810.

The server is part of the name services maintained by the Network Information Center at SRI International on behalf of the Defense Communications Agency.
sections.plainLanguage: The server provides records that programs can use to match internet names with addresses. The records follow the format described in RFC 810.

sections.title: Queries and Responses
sections.content:
A client sends a text query with a command key, arguments and optional options. HNAME searches by name, HADDR searches by address, and ALL requests the entire host table. The client connects to SRI-NIC on TCP port 101 or uses NCP socket 101 for the initial connection.

Responses use keys such as NET, GATEWAY and HOST. A multiple-record response is bracketed by BEGIN and END, and continuation lines begin with a space. Errors use ERR with a short code and a text explanation; the code can be used by a program to handle some errors automatically.
sections.plainLanguage: Ask by host name, address, or request the whole table. The server labels each returned record, and marks a multi-record list with BEGIN and END.

sections.title: Central Table as an Interim Step
sections.content:
The server uses a single global host name and address database maintained by the NIC. The RFC describes this database as an extension of the older ARPANET Hosts.txt file.

The authors call central administration with this simple server an interim solution on the way to a decentralized, distributed name and address translation service. RFC 953 is listed in the unit metadata as the RFC that later obsoleted RFC 811.
sections.plainLanguage: The server relies on one centrally maintained database. The RFC presents this as a temporary step toward a distributed lookup service.

references.text: Feinler, E., Harrenstien, K., Su, Z. and White, V., "Official DoD Internet Host Table Specification," RFC 810, March 1, 1982.
